stories.title: Jio's IPO: ₹30,000 crore, India's biggest ever, at up to ₹1,119 a share
stories.label: RISING
stories.window: Sat 10 Oct to listing on Wed 28 Oct. The next turns: RHP expected Mon 12 Oct (confirms the band), anchor book 19 Oct, open 21–23 Oct, listing 28 Oct.
happening: New since we sent it: on Friday 9 October Bloomberg reported that Jio Platforms will price its IPO at ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 a share. At the top of the band it raises about ₹30,213 crore, which would make it India's largest IPO, ahead of Hyundai Motor India.
At that price Jio would be worth about ₹10.3 lakh crore ($107 billion): India's third-biggest company, after its own parent Reliance and Bharti Airtel.
Dates, per market sources: anchor book Monday 19 Oct; open Wednesday 21 Oct to Friday 23 Oct; listing 28 Oct. The red herring prospectus, which fixes the band officially, is expected on Monday.
The grey market is quoting a premium of ₹175–180 a share, up from ₹145–150 earlier in the week: about 16% over the top of the band (unofficial).
Friday was reported as the last day to buy a Reliance share and qualify for the shareholders' quota.

Context: India's IPO market has raised over $13 billion (₹1.26 lakh crore) this year; September was a record month (34 companies, more than ₹39,300 crore), while foreign investors sold about ₹2.7 lakh crore of listed shares.
curiosity_gaps: Almost every viewer pays Jio every month. From 21 October they can own a piece of it. What exactly are they buying, and how big is ₹10.3 lakh crore next to the companies they already know?
The biggest IPO India has ever had arrives in the same week the market hit a 32-month low. Foreign investors are selling listed shares and still queuing for IPOs. Why?
The grey market already prices a 16% first-day gain. The herd question: can a ₹10 lakh crore giant actually pop on listing day?
measured: Trend meter: FLAT on news (32 items today, 97 this week); YouTube this week 334K views, top video CA Rachana Ranade's explainer (156K in 72 h).

vidIQ "jio ipo" (India): about 71,700 searches a month in India, +66% on its 30-day baseline. Competition 58 of 100. Views per hour on the keyword rose every day this week: 29K (4 Oct) to 90K (8 Oct).
Instagram outliers: two Jio IPO reels broke out (4.7M and 1.1M), both on the "it's coming" announcement.

facts.text: Price band ₹1,065–1,119 (Bloomberg report); issue about ₹30,213 crore, India's largest IPO, surpassing Hyundai Motor India; valuation about $107 bn (₹10.3 lakh crore), third-biggest company after Reliance and Bharti Airtel; anchor 19 Oct, open 21 Oct, close 23 Oct, listing 28 Oct; RHP likely Monday; GMP ₹175–180 (from ₹145–150 earlier in the week), about 16% over the upper band; Friday the last day to buy RIL shares for the shareholder quota; FIIs sold about ₹2.7 lakh crore this year; September record, 34 companies, more than ₹39,300 crore; YTD IPO fundraising above $13 bn (₹1.26 lakh crore).
The original report: Jio Platforms set to price its shares at ₹1,065–1,119, per people familiar with the matter (headline and summary; paywalled).

watch_out: No call on applying: not "apply", not "skip", no listing-gain promise. GMP is unofficial grey-market talk; if used, say it as what the grey market is quoting.
The band, size and dates are reported, not confirmed. The RHP (expected Monday) can change them: post today as "reported", or wait for the RHP and say it as fact.
Mukesh and Akash Ambani: no AI face or voice. A licensed still or their own real footage only (CLAUDE.md rule 4); the Jio logo is fine on a reel about Jio.
Tests it can carry: hook in frame one (₹30,000 crore or ₹1,119 on screen), tight 20–30 s, a line worth sending (the SIM in your pocket is now for sale).

stories.title: The UPI fee due on Thursday may be pushed to 1 January
stories.label: HOT
stories.window: Sat 10 to Thu 15 Oct. A final decision is expected "in the coming days"; if it is announced, the story turns into a one-day follow-up that evening.
happening: From Thursday 15 October, shops were due to pay a 0.4% fee (MDR) on UPI payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 a payment. It would end the zero-fee UPI the country has had since 2020. Customers don't pay it, and merchants are not allowed to pass it on.

New on 8 October: a proposal to push the start to 1 January 2027 is under consideration, after pushback from traders. It would keep shop payments free through the festive season. A final decision is expected in the coming days.
Also under consideration: exempting every business with turnover up to ₹40 lakh a year (today's exemption is only for small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month on their QR).

The traders' fight: two associations called a "No UPI Day" for 2 October, then withdrew it after meeting the Finance Minister on 30 September. The distributors' federation estimates the fee would cost FMCG distribution and retail ₹7,000–9,000 crore a year.
The government told the Supreme Court about 96% of merchant payments would be untouched. UPI handled 24.07 billion payments worth ₹29.37 lakh crore in September.
curiosity_gaps: Who actually pays? The rule says the shop pays and can't pass it on. Will your kirana really swallow ₹12 on a ₹3,000 bill, or will "cash only above ₹2,000" signs appear?
The fee was set to start in the middle of the festive season. It is being delayed for the shopkeepers' Diwali, not the customer's.
Who gets the 0.4%? The banks and the UPI app take their cut (0.28% to the payer's bank, 0.08% to the app). Free UPI was never free to run.
measured: Trend meter: HOT. "UPI charges": 8 news items today against 32 this week; YouTube this week 273K views, top video "UPI Charges Postponed?" (120K in 24 h).

vidIQ "upi charges" (India): about 137,900 searches a month; competition 63 of 100. Views per hour on the keyword peaked at 2.36M on 16 Sep (the fee announced), fell to 25K on 7 Oct and jumped back to 73K on 8 Oct with the deferral news.
YouTube Shorts on the deferral: News18 Tamil Nadu's 19 s Short is at 231K (5,768 views an hour).

stories.others_takeaway: The No UPI Day warnings went to tens of millions of views two weeks ago. The deferral is so far only on news channels' Shorts, mostly in regional languages; no Hinglish creator reel on "the fee is off till January" yet. Note: our own X1 (28 Sep, "96% UPI abhi bhi free") covered the fee itself, so this needs the new turn, not the rule.

facts.text: Rollout set for 15 Oct may move to 1 Jan 2027 (Business Standard report; decision "in the coming days"); NPCI-headed UPI and Services Steering Committee met 7 Oct; 0.40% on P2M payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300; ₹5 flat for bill payments, utilities, education, fuel; ₹40 lakh turnover exemption under consideration; existing exemption up to ₹1 lakh a month on QR; merchants pay, consumers nothing; about 96% of merchant transactions unaffected (Centre to the Supreme Court); fee split 0.28% to issuing bank, 0.12% onward, 0.08% to the UPI app; No UPI Day for 2 Oct withdrawn after meeting the FM on 30 Sep; AICPDF estimate ₹7,000–9,000 cr a year; September: 24.07 bn transactions worth ₹29.37 lakh crore.
NPCI FAQ examples: nil on ₹2,000; ₹12 on ₹3,000; ₹200 on ₹50,000; ₹300 cap from ₹75,000; merchants may not pass the charge on to customers; effective 15 Oct 2026 (FAQ dated 15 Sep; context).
The original deferral report (not opened: paywalled).

watch_out: The deferral is a proposal, not a decision. Until it is announced, 15 October still stands; say "may be pushed", not "postponed".
Customers don't pay the fee. Say it plainly; the viral reels that implied UPI would cost the user were wrong.
Humour on the system (a fee timed for Diwali, then delayed for Diwali), never on shopkeepers or the viewer.
Tests it can carry: hook in frame one (0.4% or ₹300 on screen), tight 20–30 s, a line worth sending ("your kirana pays, not you").

stories.title: Inox Clean: revenue up 43X in a year, debt up 45X, and a ₹10,000 crore IPO on hold
stories.label: COLD
stories.window: About two weeks; it returns when SEBI clears or rejects the draft papers.
happening: The Ken (9 Oct): Inox Clean Energy made 11 acquisitions since June 2025, the biggest Vena Energy for ₹6,000 crore. Its revenue went from ₹47 crore to about ₹2,000 crore in FY26 (43X) and its borrowings from ₹350 crore to nearly ₹16,000 crore (45X). Interest is now about ₹1,000 crore a year, up from about ₹30 crore.
It filed for a ₹10,000 crore IPO on 29 September: ₹8,000 crore of new shares plus ₹2,000 crore sold by promoter Devansh Jain. ₹6,000 crore of the new money goes to repaying debt.

SEBI has kept its observations on the draft papers in abeyance (reported 6 Oct). Reported reason: investigations involving INOXGFL group companies, including a group firm's sale of its Inox Clean stake that the board approved at ₹290 crore and the books show as ₹90 crore received. The group says the other ₹200 crore repaid a loan.

The draft papers also disclose that the promoter was summoned in SEBI's investigation into trading in PVR INOX shares, and that Inox Wind was summoned over its disclosures. Not a rejection; no show-cause notice as of filing.
curiosity_gaps: A company that was ₹47 crore of revenue two years ago now wants ₹10,000 crore from the public, and most of it pays back the loans that made it big. How do you grow 43X in a year? You buy the growth on credit.
SEBI has quietly paused India's next big green-energy IPO, and the papers name a probe into trading in PVR INOX, the cinema chain every viewer has been to.
The ₹290 crore that became ₹90 crore: one number the regulator wants explained.
measured: Trend meter: no news today, 5 items this week; YouTube's "HOT" reading is general market videos, not this story.
vidIQ outlier search: nobody has made a reel on it. Adjacent: a reel mocking pre-IPO hype in the unlisted market did 1.8M.

stories.others_takeaway: Nobody has made it. The documents-explained shape travels, and IPO hype is this month's biggest money conversation (Jio); this is the other side of it.

facts.text: 11 acquisitions since June 2025; largest Vena Energy, ₹6,000 crore; revenue about ₹2,000 crore in FY26 from ₹47 crore (43X); borrowings nearly ₹16,000 crore from ₹350 crore (45X); interest about ₹1,000 crore a year from about ₹30 crore; ₹10,000 crore IPO, SEBI hold; 60% for debt (headline and public text; paywalled).

SEBI kept observations in abeyance (Moneycontrol, 6 Oct); DRHP filed 29 Sep; ₹8,000 crore fresh plus ₹2,000 crore OFS by Devansh Jain; ₹6,000 crore for debt; borrowings ₹16,781.8 crore (Aug 2026); ₹290 crore approved vs ₹90 crore in the books, ₹200 crore said to repay a PFC loan; Jain summoned in the PVR Inox share-trading probe; Inox Wind summoned; not a rejection.
Reported FY26 revenue in the draft papers ₹178.1 crore (from ₹47.2 crore); profit ₹30.9 crore (from ₹1.5 crore).

watch_out: The numbers disagree: the draft papers report FY26 revenue of ₹178.1 crore (3.8X); The Ken's ₹2,000 crore (43X) appears to count the acquired businesses for the full year. Say "The Ken calculates 43X", and credit The Ken in the caption.
No wrongdoing has been found. SEBI has paused, not rejected; the promoter's summons is in a probe, not a charge. Say "SEBI wants answers", never "fraud".
No buy/sell: the IPO isn't open. No face of the promoter (no licensed photo checked).
Tests it can carry: hook in frame one (43X), tight 20–30 s; a line worth sending is weaker (stake is "some day").
